claims.claim: Regulation II 235.7(a)(1) bars issuers and networks from restricting the networks available for a debit transaction to fewer than two unaffiliated networks.
claims.quote: restrict the number of payment card networks on which an electronic debit transaction may be processed to less than two unaffiliated networks.
claims.title: 12 CFR 235.7 - Limitations on payment card restrictions
claims.publisher: Cornell LII (mirror of eCFR text)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: LII reproduces the CFR text; same text confirmed in the eCFR API point-in-time 2026-09-01.

claims.claim: 235.7(a)(3) forbids a network from limiting an issuer's ability to contract with any other network that could process its debit transactions.
claims.quote: a payment card network may not restrict or otherwise limit an issuer's ability to contract with any other payment card network
claims.title: 12 CFR 235.7 - Limitations on payment card restrictions
claims.publisher: Cornell LII (mirror of eCFR text)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: 235.7(b) prohibits issuers and networks from inhibiting a merchant's ability to direct routing over any network that can process the transaction.
claims.quote: inhibit the ability of any person that accepts or honors debit cards for payments to direct the routing of electronic debit transactions
claims.title: 12 CFR 235.7 - Limitations on payment card restrictions
claims.publisher: Cornell LII (mirror of eCFR text)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The official commentary lists card-not-present as a 'particular type of transaction' for which two unaffiliated networks must be enabled.
claims.quote: particular type of transaction ( e.g., card-not-present transaction) for which the issuer's debit card can be used to perform an electronic debit transaction
claims.title: eCFR Title 12 Part 235 - Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing (Regulation II), point-in-time 2026-09-01
claims.publisher: eCFR (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Commentary example: an issuer may comply with networks A (CP and CNP), B (CP only) and C (CNP only).

claims.claim: The Board's October 2022 final rule requiring two unaffiliated networks for card-not-present debit transactions took effect July 1, 2023.
claims.quote: The final rule will be effective July 1, 2023.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board finalizes updates to the Board's rule concerning debit card transactions
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Board said the 2022 routing rule would push networks to compete and improve fraud-prevention capabilities, and did not alter interchange caps.
claims.quote: The final rule will encourage competition between networks and incentivize them to improve their fraud-prevention capabilities.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board finalizes updates to the Board's rule concerning debit card transactions
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The interchange cap in force as of September 2026 remains 21 cents plus 5 basis points of transaction value (235.3).
claims.quote: is no more than the sum of— (1) 21 cents and; (2) 5 basis points multiplied by the value of the transaction.
claims.title: eCFR Title 12 Part 235 - Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing (Regulation II), point-in-time 2026-09-01
claims.publisher: eCFR (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Point-in-time eCFR as of 2026-09-01 still shows the 2011 amounts, i.e. the October 2023 proposal has not been finalized into the CFR.

claims.claim: A covered issuer may add a fraud-prevention adjustment of no more than 1 cent per transaction (235.4).
claims.quote: an issuer may receive or charge an amount of no more than 1 cent per transaction in addition to any interchange
claims.title: eCFR Title 12 Part 235 - Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing (Regulation II), point-in-time 2026-09-01
claims.publisher: eCFR (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Issuers with under $10 billion in assets (with affiliates) are exempt from the interchange cap but not from routing rules (235.5).
claims.quote: The issuer, together with its affiliates, has assets of less than $10 billion as of the end of the calendar year preceding
claims.title: eCFR Title 12 Part 235 - Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing (Regulation II), point-in-time 2026-09-01
claims.publisher: eCFR (Office of the Federal Register)
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Board's October 2023 proposal would cut the base component to 14.4 cents, ad valorem to 4.0 bp and the fraud adjustment to 1.3 cents.
claims.quote: the base component would be 14.4 cents, the ad valorem component would be 4.0 basis points (multiplied by the value of the transaction)
claims.title: Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing (Proposed Rule, Docket R-1818, RIN 7100-AG67)
claims.publisher: Federal Register
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fraud-prevention adjustment would be 1.3 cents; amounts to apply until June 30, 2025, then update every other year from the biennial issuer survey.

claims.claim: The Board framed the proposal as lowering the cap on a $50 transaction from 24.5 cents to 17.7 cents, with biennial automatic updates.
claims.quote: the cap on an average-sized $50 debit card transaction would decline from 24.5 cents under the current rule to 17.7 cents under the proposal.
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposal to lower the maximum interchange fee
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The comment period on the 2023 interchange proposal was extended from February 12, 2024 to May 12, 2024.

claims.title: Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing; Extension of Comment Period
claims.publisher: Federal Register
claims.label: Verified
